dct_description_sm: The objective of this project is to study the occurrence and tissue distribution of microplastics, benzotriazole UV stabilizers (BZT-UVs; including UV328), organic UV filters, and chlorinated paraffins in the muscle, liver, and kidney of caribou from Yukon (Porcupine herd) and Nunavut (Qamanirjuaq herd), contributing data on plastic additives (including UV stabilizers and chlorinated paraffins) that are present in traditional foods to partners that are interested in understanding human exposure to these contaminants, and  contributing data to the current Arctic Councils Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programs (AMAP) Litter and Microplastic Expert Group (LMEG) relating to the toxicity of plastic related and derived contaminants in the Arctic. Short-term objectives include measuring plastic particles, benzotriazole UV stabilizers (BZT-UVs), a group of plastic additives, and chlorinated paraffins, a group of contaminants associated with plastics, in Porcupine and Qamanirjuaq caribou and establishing a baseline dataset for these emerging contaminants in an Arctic terrestrial food web. This research program will help to elucidate and reduce the exposure risks of Arctic caribou and humans to plastic-associated contaminants. The results will also help to evaluate the role of plastics as a vector of these contaminants in the Arctic food web.
dct_title_s: Tissue distribution of microplastics and plastic additives in Porcupine (Yukon) and Qamanirjuaq (Nunavut) caribou
